### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **7** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-package`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/kernel.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/kernel.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/kernel.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/kernel.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **150** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fd0e72abc2af5bd4d7056e7c2e387dc992d0f1df` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b3a2616e3e21b96989f39e2155250673b37d9676` — the merge of head `7c45b88c05570a1f1c50dd403a860efa14fc75d1` into base `fd0e72abc2af5bd4d7056e7c2e387dc992d0f1df`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b3a2616e3e21b96989f39e2155250673b37d9676 && git checkout b3a2616e3e21b96989f39e2155250673b37d9676
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fd0e72abc2af5bd4d7056e7c2e387dc992d0f1df 7c45b88c05570a1f1c50dd403a860efa14fc75d1 && git checkout -B drift-repro fd0e72abc2af5bd4d7056e7c2e387dc992d0f1df && git merge --no-ff 7c45b88c05570a1f1c50dd403a860efa14fc75d1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fd0e72abc2af5bd4d7056e7c2e387dc992d0f1df
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fd0e72abc2af5bd4d7056e7c2e387dc992d0f1df` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `410897be9de2e223fc3aa550c6180ae3fb9bbbbe`
Local-runs: none

Inputs, and nothing else: card #23972 (body; comments 6219421613 triage, 6220830814 claim, 6222511724 os-dev-report), PR #24010 (body, its 75-file list, the net diff against `main` at merge base `92fd343bcf`), and the 41 check-runs on the head, re-read immediately before this record was rendered: 36 success, 5 skipped by path or schedule (Console Pin Gate, Temporal Conformance, the Dogfood shard and Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke), 0 failure, 0 in progress; Test Core 1/6 through 6/6 all success. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing was built, run or re-run here. Ruling of record: Ruling B on #23892 (6216295104) item 1, as the claim quotes it. Served tier: the file list carries published schemas (`packages/spec/src/**/*.zod.ts`), so the schema face.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the net diff implies, each named right or wrong:

1. `InstalledPackageSourceSchema` (`z.enum(['code', 'marketplace', 'authored'])`) and `InstalledPackageSource` (`z.input`), two new exports of `@objectstack/spec/kernel` — RIGHT. The set is ruling B item 1's closed set verbatim, no fourth value, no default. ADR-0122 isomorphism pinned (788 → 789 in `type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts`); `api-surface`, `export-origins`, `declaration-map` and `json-schema.manifest` regenerated, and `check:generated` sits inside the green Lint gates.
2. `InstalledPackageSchema.source`, REQUIRED with no default — RIGHT as a contract: declare equals enforce, every row has an origin, and it is pinned (three values accepted; `cloud` refused at `source` with `invalid_value`; a source-less row refused at `source`). Its DIRECTION is a narrowing of a published accept set: `package-api.test.ts`'s own diff turns eleven fixtures `{ manifest: validManifest }` that parsed at the merge base into refusals until `source: 'code'` is added; `authorable-surface/kernel.json` and `api.json` gained `kernel/InstalledPackage:source` and `api/AssembledInstalledPackage:source`, so the repo's own generator lists it as an author-written key; and the published JSON-schema manifest carries the new required key to every external validator. Judged in ②.
3. The served row: `InstalledPackageAtEitherStageSchema` is now the union of `InstalledPackageSchema.extend({ writable })` and `AssembledInstalledPackageSchema.extend({ writable })`, `writable: z.boolean()` required on both branches; `ListInstalledPackagesResponseSchema` and `GetInstalledPackageResponseSchema` carry both keys by reference (`package-api.zod.ts` declares only the request halves; its `:478` install response references the record schema, so `source` yes and `writable` no, which is what the registry returns) — RIGHT. Measured against the runtime at the head: both read doors apply `withWritableVerdict` (`packages.ts:1150` list, `:2207` detail) and `INSTALLED_PACKAGE_RESPONSE_FIELDS` projects `source` off the record with no derivation, which is the claim's "no join". Pinned: the served body parses through its declared contract with `source` and `writable` kept (`packages-writable-verdict.test.ts`), and the record schemas strip `writable` (`package-api.test.ts`). Direction: the served row GREW two keys, and the row validator now REFUSES a `writable`-less or `source`-less row. Both facts hold; judged in ②.
4. `SchemaRegistry.installPackage(manifest, source, settings?, scope?)` in `@objectstack/objectql`, a published class — the origin as a required second positional, refused by `TypeError` before any mutation (pinned: no row, no namespace claim, in `package-source-stamp.test.ts`) — RIGHT as the record seam: the registry records and never infers. Direction: BREAKING for every pre-existing caller: `installPackage(manifest)` throws, and `installPackage(manifest, settings, scope)` hands `settings` to the enum parse and throws. The PR body names it an "API change" and the changeset ships a FROM → TO table for it. Judged in ②.
5. `EngineSchemaRegistryView.installPackage(manifest, source, settings?)` in `@objectstack/spec/contracts` — the same insertion at the contract level; the spelled union is held equal to `InstalledPackageSource` by a type-level pin (`objectql-engine.test.ts`) — RIGHT as a contract, with the same breaking direction as 4. Note, not blocking: the contract's `registerApp(manifest: any): void` at `:437` is untouched, so a contract-level caller cannot state an origin; the `manifest` service door carries it instead.
6. `ObjectQL.registerApp(body, scope?, source = 'code')` and the `manifest` service's `register(artifact, { source? })` — optional, additive, default `code`; `authored` refused with nothing recorded (pinned); every package of a multi-package marketplace artifact stamped (pinned) — RIGHT.
7. Producer inventory, verified against the head tree, non-test source only: every `registry.installPackage` caller passes a source (`protocol.ts:31395` authored; `engine.ts:7922` through `registerApp`; runtime `packages.ts:1414` authored; `service-package/src/index.ts:718` authored). Every source-less `manifest.register` caller is a plugin's own bundle, so `code` is its meaning: `cloud-connection-plugin.ts:212` (`CLOUD_CONNECTION_UI_BUNDLE`), `marketplace-proxy-plugin.ts:208` (`MARKETPLACE_BROWSE_UI_BUNDLE`), `metadata-protocol/src/plugin.ts:221` (`com.objectstack.metadata-objects`), `runtime/src/app-plugin.ts:575` (the host bundle), and the services' and plugins' own manifests. The install-local plugin states `marketplace` on the hot register (`:1557`) and on the ledger rehydrate (`:783`), pinned on both halves with the plugin's own UI bundle as the control leg — RIGHT.
8. Persistence: `sys_packages` stores `id, version, manifest, metadata, hash` (`package-table.ts:127`, `:161`); the record is not persisted, so "no new storage" holds. `protocol.ts` is its only writer, so a marketplace row cannot return through the authored rehydrate, and the rehydrate stamps `authored` (pinned in `hydration.test.ts`) — RIGHT.
9. `SchemaRegistry.validate('package', item)` (`registry.ts:4869`) parses through the record schema and now refuses a source-less item; at its one call site (`:4694`) it is a logged diagnostic, not a gate, and no in-repo producer registers a `package`-typed item through that door — note only.
10. `@objectstack/client`: docblocks only; the row types flow from spec; the `packages-write-envelope` and `return-type-precision` pins carry `writable` — RIGHT.
11. Liveness: no hand-kept ledger row exists for `InstalledPackage` keys and `Spec property liveness` is green on the head, so the claim's "liveness rows the change moves" names none — nothing owed.

### ② Semver level

- Bumps: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/objectql` minor, the other five patch. The LEVELS are right: under the launch-window rule (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`) a breaking change ships as `minor`, so `minor` is the ceiling for spec and objectql; the patch packages publish behaviour (the stamps) and no surface of their own; client is docblocks.
- The direction line, spelled `yes (widening)` on the PR body, the claim and the changeset body — WRONG on the arm. The diff widens one surface (the served row gains `source` and `writable`; two new kernel exports) and narrows others: the record and served-row schemas refuse what they accepted at the merge base (judgments 2 and 3; the PR's own fixture churn is the measurement), and `SchemaRegistry.installPackage` plus the `EngineSchemaRegistryView` contract break every pre-existing call (judgments 4 and 5). `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` spells this exact case: "`yes (narrowing)` — a diff that widens one surface and narrows another. Both facts are true and both are read." AGENTS.md §3: `(narrowing)` is BREAKING; a breaking changeset must carry its migration, which is present (the two FROM → TO tables), AND exactly one `adr-0087:` disposition marker in the changeset body, which is ABSENT. With `(widening)`, `check-adr-0087-registration` read no breaking signal (no `major`, no `**BREAKING`, no `!`, no narrowing arm) and asked for no disposition, so its green says nothing about direction; that is the #16296 shape the arm was added to close. The dev's axis-4 argument (no external reader of the record schema named) is not the arm's question: the arm reads the published accept set, not a roster of readers.
- What the diff needs before a PASS: the three carriers (PR body, claim, changeset) re-spelled `yes (narrowing)` on the direction line, and one `adr-0087:` disposition marker in the changeset body (the HTML-comment form ADR-0087's 2026-08-13 addendum spells; `check-adr-0087-registration` prints the closed vocabulary when it fails). Of that vocabulary, by the gate's own stated refusals: `unpublished` is refused (every bumped package publishes); `no-migration-prescription` and `runtime-interface-only` are refused by a body that carries FROM → TO; `type-surface-only` needs a narrowing off `any`, which this is not. So the remaining honest routes are `registered` with an ADR-0087 ledger entry (the route ADR-0112 took for a wire-only narrowing), or a seat ruling on the card, in writing, that re-grades the arm. Nothing else in the diff needs to move.

### ③ Boundary flags

Deviations, five, from the os-dev-report:

1. `writable` on the SERVED row, not on `InstalledPackageSchema` — RIGHT. The card's own ask was "declare `writable` on the response schema"; the registry never stores it (`withWritableVerdict` computes it per read); pinned that the record schemas strip it. The claim's first bullet was the imprecise one.
2. Files outside the claim's surface (client docblocks and one client pin, the registry contract, the ADR-0122 pin, the client patch) — RIGHT, each necessary and explained in the report; the contract file is where judgment 5 lands.
3. The contract spells `'code' | 'marketplace' | 'authored'` instead of importing it — ACCEPTED: a second spelling of the closed set, held equal by a type-level pin, with the `gen:skill-refs` closure reason measured rather than asserted.
4. About 100 test call sites of `registry.installPackage` now pass a source — mechanical, RIGHT.
5. `origin/main` `92fd343b` merged into the branch before the PR opened — AGENTS.md §10; the merge base of record is `92fd343bcf` and the net diff is 75 files, equal to the PR's file list.

Open questions, three:

1. Should the arm read `(narrowing)` for the record schema's accept set? ANSWERED, B: relabel `yes (narrowing)` and add the ADR-0087 disposition marker. The reasons are ②'s, and this is the one defect behind the verdict. Not escalated: the rule is written (AGENTS.md §3, `clause2-line.mjs`), so no ruling is needed to apply it.
2. Should `registerApp` require `source` instead of defaulting to `code`? ANSWERED, A: keep the default. Verified at the head (judgment 7) that every in-repo producer on that door whose origin is not `code` is install-local, and it is stamped on both halves. The hosted-kernel loader outside this repository (the report's "carrier: none" note) is ESCALATED to the seat as a cloud-side follow-up; it is not this PR's.
3. The two `source` / `writable` divergences. (1) `POST /packages` with `manifest.scope` `system` or `cloud` serving `authored` with `writable: false` — ANSWERED, B, note only: each key is honest on its own (`source` says who registered, `writable` what this server allows), and the schema docblock now says they are two statements. (2) `POST /packages?overwrite=true` over an id code registered, the row re-stamped `authored` while the boot map keeps it read-only — ESCALATED to the seat as a candidate card after a public-door reproduction; the report's own out-of-scope finding names it with reach not measured. Neither blocks this PR.

Not blocking, for the seat after landing: the contract's `registerApp(manifest: any)` carries no origin parameter (judgment 5), and the objectui follow-up (the Source column reads `row.source` and drops the two-read join) stays to be filed.

Reviewed-by: `session_01LFqdRsuM5nkqoJdHd5ztVk`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7c45b88c05570a1f1c50dd403a860efa14fc75d1`
Local-runs: probe — readClause2Line from scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs applied to the three carriers' Clause-② lines, to read the arm the way check-adr-0087-registration reads it; nothing built, tested or re-run
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/package-api-assembled.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/objectql-engine.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/package-registry.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.installed-package-row-source-required.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.registry-install-package-source-argument.ts + .changeset/23972-installed-package-source.md, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template, packages/spec/scripts/build-migration-registry.ts, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md

DELTA review after contract review FAIL `6222834057` on `410897be9d`. Inputs, and nothing else: card #23972 (body; comments 6219421613 triage, 6220830814 claim as edited 19:14Z, 6222511724 round-1 report, 6223094149 round-2 report), PR #24010 (body as edited by the seat 19:29Z, its 77-file list, the net diff against `main` at merge base `92fd343bcf`), and the 46 check-runs on the head, re-read at 19:36Z immediately before this record was rendered. By the newest run of each of the 39 check names: 25 success, 7 skipped by path or schedule (Console Pin Gate, Temporal Conformance, the Dogfood shard and Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, and the re-run Auto Label and Check PR Size, whose first runs were success), 0 failure, 7 in progress. NOT MEASURED, in progress at render time and not waited for: Test Core 1/6 through 6/6 and Type Check · workspace. Measured and success: Check Changeset on both runs (19:28Z on the head, and 19:30Z after the PR-body edit; this job hosts check-adr-0087-registration against the merge base), Type Check · source gates (hosts check:spec-changes and check:upgrade-guide), Build Core, Build Docs, every Lint job, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, the claim, single-writer and part-of checks. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing was built, run or re-run here beyond the one probe named above. Ruling of record: Ruling B on #23892 (6216295104) item 1, as the claim quotes it. Served tier: the file list carries published schemas, so the schema face; record-recognisers reads the same face off the 77 paths.

Round 2 is one commit, `7c45b88c05`, three files: the changeset (modified) and two new semantic ledger entries. Nothing else moved: both heads share the merge base `92fd343bcf`, and `git diff` from that base to each head with the three round-2 paths excluded hashes identical (sha256 `5501bab612ed…`), so the 75 round-1 paths are byte-identical and the file list is 77 = 75 + 2. Record 6222834057's section ① judgments 1 through 11 carry over unchanged and are adopted here; the new judgments below are numbered on from them.

### ① Derived judgments

12. Ledger entry `installed-package-row-source-required` (step 18) — RIGHT. Surface: `InstalledPackageSchema.source` on every installed-package row, required and closed to code / marketplace / authored, and `writable` on the served `GET /api/v1/packages` and `GET /api/v1/packages/:id` row (`InstalledPackageAtEitherStageSchema`), required. That is exactly judgments 2 and 3 of the earlier record: the record schema and the served-row union refuse what they accepted at the merge base, the install response (`package-api.zod.ts:478`) references the record schema and so carries `source` but not `writable`, and the entry names only the two GET doors for `writable`, which is the precise set. Replacement: read `row.source` and `row.writable` as served; stated "not mechanically convertible" for a row held elsewhere, because a reader cannot invent the origin and only the registering door knows it — honest, and it is the same argument the PR body and changeset make. Reason: the per-door stamping (code at registerApp, marketplace at install-local's install and ledger rehydrate, authored at installPackage and the sys_packages rehydrate) matches the producer inventory verified in judgment 7, and the "join reads a control-plane install as code wherever install-local is off" edge is the card body's own. Acceptance criteria: checkable by parse (every row through `InstalledPackageSchema` carries a closed-set `source`; every served row through the union carries a boolean `writable`) and by grep (no reader derives origin from `writable` or a second list; an unattributable row is re-read, not guessed). `relevantWhen` omitted, so the entry is always listed: an installed-package row is not a top-level stack key, so no structured question could prove it absent, which is the "never silence" default the type's own docblock prescribes.
13. Ledger entry `registry-install-package-source-argument` (step 18) — RIGHT, one note. Surface: `SchemaRegistry.installPackage` in `@objectstack/objectql` and `EngineSchemaRegistryView.installPackage` in `@objectstack/spec/contracts`, the origin inserted as the second positional — judgments 4 and 5 of the earlier record. Replacement: pass the origin second, move settings and scope one position right, prefer `registerApp` or the manifest service's `register(artifact, { source })` where they fit; "not mechanically convertible: only the caller knows the origin, so no codemod can choose it" — honest: a codemod can insert a slot but cannot pick the value, which is the thing the contract requires. Reason: `TypeError` before anything is recorded (pinned, `package-source-stamp.test.ts`), and the settings-read-as-origin failure for the old three-argument call, both verified at the head (`registry.ts:5440`).
